_comment: Single source of truth for satoshistatues.com. Edit here, then run: python3 build.py

config._proof_of_walk_help: Proof of Walk passport ranks: /proof-of-walk/ and /proof-of-walk/fellow-travelers/, data from the Worker /api/pow/* (POW_ENABLED). enabled=true: pages built, plus small links in the check-in note, the leaderboard and the home passport. preview=true: pages are noindex and left out of the sitemap. Ranks (Noah 2026-10-30 12:35 ET): Confirmed (first GPS stamp); Genesis Block = GPS stamps at any genesis_required (3) of genesis_set (the FIXED original 10, never add to it); The Grand High Order of Fellow Travelers = Genesis + order_extra (1) more statue anywhere on the map. order_keep: true = the Order is kept for good once earned. Order members are ranked by total statues stamped, ties to whoever got there first. All of these reach the Worker via build.py --worker. enabled=false: no pages, no links.
config._lodging_help: Stay nearby (BTC Map lodging, tools/fetch_merchants.py → lodging.json): up to max_items stays within radius_mi miles; if none, the nearest within fallback_km (labelled); else a one-line none. Re-run the fetch after changing. The fetch drops dead stay websites automatically (404/410, no such domain, parked/placeholder page); hide_websites lists extra dead links confirmed by hand (shown with their BTC Map link instead).
config._nostr_help: Nostr profile for the site. nostr_hex is served as NIP-05 _@satoshistatues.com via /.well-known/nostr.json. Then run: python3 build.py
config._photo_help: Visitor photos are not collected by email: statue pages and map popups ask people to post their own photo and tag us (handles in build.py SOCIAL_TAGS). photo_x_handle is still used for photo credits/shoutouts.
config._leaderboard_help: Leaderboard API (Cloudflare Worker in /workspace/leaderboard). Statue coordinates for its server-side distance check come from `python3 build.py --worker`.

statues.name: Budapest
statues.note: World’s first Satoshi statue. Reflective face so visitors see themselves (“We are all Satoshi”). Free public access 24/7.
statues.access: Outdoors in Graphisoft Park. Can be visited 24/7, free of charge (per the statue’s official site).
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Budapest

visit.getting_there:
From OpenStreetMap (straight-line distances; lines and timetables unverified): the nearest bus stops are Sujtás utca (about 400 m) and Záhony utca (about 470 m). The nearest rail stops are the Aquincum railway halt (about 780 m) and the Kaszásdűlő HÉV suburban-rail stop (about 800 m).

Parking: OpenStreetMap shows a 120-space surface lot about 180 m away. Whether it's public or for park tenants only is unverified.
visit.exact_spot:
In Graphisoft Park, Záhony u. 7, 1031 Budapest (District III), per the official site. Köztérkép, the Hungarian public-art register, places it on the green area in front of the Microsoft building, facing the Heracles (Herkules) statue. In OpenStreetMap, the Herkules statue is about 15 m away and the Microsoft office about 40 m. Pin: 47.56072, 19.05438 (OpenStreetMap node 9843217531).

It is not in City Park (Városliget), despite what some listings say.
visit.photo_tip:
This isn't a see-through design. The face is a polished bronze-aluminium composite, so every visitor can see their own face in it (official site).

Generic tip (not from a source): shoot close so your reflection sits inside the hood, and keep the sun behind you to avoid flare.
visit.hours_access: Outdoors. The official site says it can be visited 24/7, free of charge.

story.label: Artists
story.text: Réka Gergely and Tamás Gilly, Hungarian sculptors.

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 16 Sep 2021, in Graphisoft Park, Budapest.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Founders from the Hungarian crypto community: András Györfi (Kripto Akadémia, who came up with the idea), Gabi Debreczeni-Raskó and Barnabás Debreczeni (MrCoin), Imre Szilágyi (Blockchain Budapest) and Kornél Kalocsai (Blockchain Hungary Association). It was community-funded.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: A generic human figure in a hoodie with the Bitcoin logo on the chest, because Satoshi's gender, race, age and height are unknown. The face is reflective, so every visitor sees themselves in it: "We are all Satoshi".

story.label: Materials
story.text: Bronze, with a face of bronze-aluminium composite.

story.label: Notable
story.text: Widely described as the world's first statue of Satoshi Nakamoto.

statues.name: Lugano
statues.note: First of the optical-illusion series. Unveiled in Parco Ciani in Oct 2024, it was later moved to the Foce, the mouth of the Cassarate river, where vandals threw it into Lake Lugano on the night of 1–2 Aug 2025; divers recovered it in pieces. The artist repaired it with the kintsugi technique and it was re-inaugurated on 24 Oct 2025 in the central area of Parco Ciani, near the Dying Socrates sculpture. On 19 Apr 2026 it was vandalized again and found seriously damaged in its central body. It was back on display in Parco Ciani on 22 Oct 2026, the eve of the 5th Plan ₿ Forum.
statues.access: In Parco Ciani, a public park open every day: 6:30–23:30 (March–October) and 6:30–21:00 (November–February).

sources.label: Satoshigallery on X: back on display (22 Oct 2026)

statues.label: Satoshi Statue Lugano

visit.getting_there:
From OpenStreetMap (straight-line distances from the 2024 statue position; routes unverified): the Palazzo Congressi bus stop is about 130 m away, and the Lugano Centro bus hub (TPL) about 360 m.

Parking: the paid underground Autosilo Piazza Castello is about 135 m away (OpenStreetMap).
visit.exact_spot: In Parco Ciani, Lugano's lakefront park. The statue was first installed there in Oct 2024 (pin 46.00441, 8.95659, OpenStreetMap node 12288711744), then moved to the Foce (Cassarate river mouth), where it was thrown into the lake on 1–2 Aug 2025. On 24 Oct 2025 it was re-inaugurated in the central area of Parco Ciani, near the "Dying Socrates" sculpture (Corriere del Ticino). It was damaged there again on 19 Apr 2026 and was back on display in Parco Ciani on 22 Oct 2026, on its plinth on the lakeside lawn (Satoshigallery and visitor photos on X). That exact spot may differ from the 2024 pin and is unverified.
visit.photo_tip:
It's a Satoshigallery design, so the figure reads from the side and nearly vanishes from the front.

Generic tip (not from a source): the lake makes a clean background for a head-on shot.
visit.hours_access: Back on display since 22 Oct 2026 (Satoshigallery on X; visitor photos from the Plan ₿ Forum, 23–26 Oct 2026), after it was found seriously damaged on 19 Apr 2026 (RSI; Ticinonline). It is outdoors in the park, with no admission fee mentioned. Parco Ciani itself is open daily from 6:30 to 23:30 (March–October) and 6:30 to 21:00 (November–February), per the City of Lugano.

sources.label: Visitor photos on X (24 and 26 Oct 2026)

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 25 Oct 2024, in front of Villa Ciani at the 3rd Plan ₿ Forum. Re-inaugurated on 24 Oct 2025 after repair.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Unveiled by Plan ₿, the joint initiative of Tether and the City of Lugano. Who paid for the piece has not been stated.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: It is designed to disappear as you change your viewpoint, "symbolizing Satoshi's retreat from the public eye after laying the foundation of a revolutionary financial system". It is the first statue of the 21 Nodes series.

story.label: History
story.text: After the unveiling it was moved to the Foce, at the mouth of the Cassarate river. Around 2 a.m. on Saturday 2 Aug 2025 a group of youths threw it into the lake; divers recovered it on 3 Aug. It was repaired and re-inaugurated on 24 Oct 2025 after a petition with about 1,300 signatures led by Luca Esposito (Satoshi Spritz). It was vandalized again on 19 Apr 2026 and was back on display in Parco Ciani on 22 Oct 2026.

statues.name: El Zonte
statues.note: Located in the famous Bitcoin Beach community that helped inspire El Salvador’s Bitcoin adoption. It was first shown at Museo MARTE in San Salvador around 1 Feb 2025, then moved to El Zonte in April 2025 as part of a new public space opened by the Ministry of Public Works.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue El Zonte

visit.getting_there:
We couldn't verify bus routes to El Zonte. OpenStreetMap shows an unnamed bus stop about 180 m from the statue, on the coastal road (Carretera del Litoral).

Parking: OpenStreetMap marks a surface parking area about 330 m away. Fees are unverified.
visit.exact_spot: In the public beachfront space at Playa El Zonte (Bitcoin Beach), La Libertad, which El Salvador's Ministry of Public Works opened in April 2025. Satoshigallery's own map pin is 13.4954011, -89.4424197. The Bitcoin Beach Office is about 85 m away (BTC Map/OpenStreetMap).
visit.photo_tip:
It's a Satoshigallery design, so the figure is visible from the side and nearly disappears from the front. The best angle at this site is unverified.

Generic tip (not from a source): with the sea behind it, shooting head-on makes the see-through effect obvious, and late-afternoon light is softer.
visit.hours_access: Outdoors in a public space with beach showers, water stations and a calisthenics area (El Salvador in English, citing the Ministry of Public Works). No hours or fees are published, so treat both as unverified.

sources.label: Satoshigallery map pin (via its 13 Apr 2025 post)

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: First presented at Museo MARTE in San Salvador around 1 Feb 2025 (Satoshigallery post of 1 Feb, tied to the Plan ₿ Forum El Salvador on 30–31 Jan 2025). It then moved to Bitcoin Beach, opening with a new public space on 12–13 Apr 2025.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: ChainCatcher reports that Tether and Plan ₿ unveiled it as the series' second statue, and it was installed as part of a public space built by El Salvador's Ministry of Public Works. Who paid for it has not been confirmed.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: Satoshigallery says it gives the viewer "this feeling of disappearance… the inventor is between the lines". The seated figure with a computer on its knees honours all developers, and standing behind it, the viewer "becomes Satoshi". It is engraved "We are all Satoshi" and pays tribute to El Zonte's role as Bitcoin Beach.

story.label: Series
story.text: 2nd statue of the 21 Nodes series.

statues.name: Tokyo
statues.note: Outside Tokyo Bitcoin Base near Yotsuya Station. Unveiled on 25 Apr 2025 at the Base’s grand opening.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Tokyo

visit.getting_there:
Tokyo Bitcoin Base lists its access as a 6-minute walk from Yotsuya Station, and a 9-minute walk from both Ichigaya Station and Akebonobashi Station. That's from the venue's website as archived in Nov 2025. The live site showed a maintenance notice on 2026-10-21.

Per OpenStreetMap, the nearest Yotsuya Station entrance is about 320 m away, and Akebonobashi (Toei Subway, S03) about 640 m. Parking is unverified.
visit.exact_spot: Outside Tokyo Bitcoin Base, 2-8 Yotsuya-Honshiocho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo 160-0003 (Forbes: the statue "sits outside of Tokyo Bitcoin Base"). Forbes describes the building as four stories on a relatively quiet block. Pin: 35.68897, 139.72854 (OpenStreetMap node for Tokyo Bitcoin Base).
visit.photo_tip:
It's a Satoshigallery design, so the figure is visible from the side and nearly disappears from the front. Take both angles. The exact best viewpoint at this site is unverified.

Generic tip (not from a source): it's a street-side spot, so go early or late to avoid passers-by in the frame.
visit.hours_access: The statue is outdoors outside the building. Opening hours for viewing it are unverified. Inside, the co-working space offers drop-ins on weekdays from 10:00 to 18:00 for ¥5,500 per day, with Lightning accepted, per the archived Nov 2025 site.

nearby.name: Tokyo Bitcoin Base
nearby.note: The statue's host venue, with paid drop-in co-working.

nearby.name: Cocorotus Foodtruck
nearby.note: Listed at the Base. Its archived site says the food truck runs Tue, Wed and Fri from 11:00 to 14:00.

nearby.name: Around Foodtruck
nearby.note: Also appears at other spots nearby, so its location varies.

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 25 Apr 2025, at the grand opening of Tokyo Bitcoin Base (about 100 guests).

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Tokyo Bitcoin Base, which was opened by Fulgur Ventures. Who bought the statue has not been stated.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: Seated hacker with a laptop on his lap, built from 61 thin mirror-polished stainless-steel profiles with gaps between them (a technique taken from sculptor Julian Voss-Andreae), on a Corten-steel base. It is clear from the side and almost invisible head-on, standing for Satoshi's anonymity and retreat from public life. Someone standing behind it is reflected in the face, so "We are all Satoshi". The "cliché" hacker deliberately honours all the developers who built Bitcoin. It was unveiled alongside the Base's mission to "make Japan a great Bitcoin nation again".

story.label: Series
story.text: Reported as the 3rd of the series: Forbes called it "currently just one of three in the world" at the opening.

statues.name: Hanoi
statues.place: 1Matrix HQ, Century Tower (16th floor), Times City
statues.note: Inside the Blockchain Gallery at 1Matrix headquarters, which 1Matrix lists on the 16th floor of the Century building, Times City, 458 Minh Khai (whether the gallery itself is on that floor is unverified). Reported open to the public on Saturdays in Sep 2025; hours unverified. The map pin is a third-party location for the building, so it is approximate.
statues.access: Indoors in the Blockchain Gallery at 1Matrix headquarters (Century building, Times City). Reported open to the public every Saturday (Sep 2025); hours unverified.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Hanoi

visit.getting_there:
Buses only, as far as we could verify. OpenStreetMap shows the "T1 Vinhomes Times City" (about 130 m) and "Khu đô thị Times City" (about 240 m) stops near the complex's centre. Routes and the walk to the Century building are unverified.

Parking: unverified.
visit.exact_spot: Indoors in the Blockchain Gallery at 1Matrix headquarters in Times City (Viet Nam News). 1Matrix gives its address as 16th floor, Century building, Times City, 458 Minh Khai, Hanoi. Whether the gallery is on that same floor is unverified. A third-party listing pins the Century building at about 20.99732, 105.86837 (unverified).
visit.photo_tip:
It's a Satoshigallery design: seen from an angle, Satoshi's profile is visible, and from the front it fades to near transparency (Viet Nam News). Take both angles.

Generic tip (not from a source): it's indoors, so turn off your flash to avoid glare on the metal slats.
visit.hours_access: Indoors. In Sep 2025 it was reported open to the public every Saturday (Viet Nam News; VNA), with no hours given. Confirm with 1Matrix before you go, because this hasn't been re-verified since.

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery). The Vietnam Blockchain and Digital Asset Association says she spent 21 months completing the piece.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Brought to Vietnam by the Vietnam Blockchain and Digital Asset Association (VBA; chairman Phan Đức Trung) and displayed at 1Matrix headquarters.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: It fades from the front, "symbolising Nakamoto's retreat after laying the foundation for a decentralised system". The VBA says it "represents the culture of decentralisation".

story.label: Series
story.text: Reported as the 4th Picozzi statue. Viet Nam News calls it the "fifth such artwork" worldwide, counting Budapest.

statues.name: Miami
statues.note: Unveiled on 11 Nov 2025 in Miami Beach, brought to Miami by Cantor Fitzgerald’s Brandon and Kyle Lutnick; Michael Saylor attended and helped unveil it. A permanent waterfront park location was announced but has not been named, so the map pin is approximate.
statues.access: Not yet installed at a permanent public site. A waterfront park location was announced but has not been confirmed.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Miami (Valentina Picozzi)

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: Tuesday 11 Nov 2025, at Cantor Fitzgerald's Crypto, AI & Energy Infrastructure Conference in Miami Beach. Reported: Miami New Times, published on Wednesday 12 Nov, says it was unveiled "on Tuesday".

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Brought to Miami by Cantor Fitzgerald's Brandon and Kyle Lutnick ("So proud to bring this powerful sculpture to the city of Miami"). Michael Saylor attended and helped unveil it, and Tether's Paolo Ardoino attended. Funding details have not been reported.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: A metal hacker sitting cross-legged with a laptop that "aims to give the viewer a sense of disappearance… when the observer places themselves behind the statue, they become Satoshi".

story.label: Series
story.text: 5th of the series (The Cryptonomist: "fifth installation").

story.label: Where it will go
story.text: Mayor Francis Suarez said it will be permanently displayed in "one of our greatest parks by the water". No park has been named, and we found no report of its installation.

visit.exact_spot: Not installed yet. Miami Mayor Francis Suarez said it will be permanently displayed in "one of our greatest parks by the water", but no park has been named, and we found no report of its installation (searched Oct 2026). The map pin is a generic Miami city-centre point, not a statue site.
visit.hours_access: Not yet installed at a public site, so there is nothing to visit yet. Directions will be added once a permanent site is announced.

alert.title: Not installed yet · approximate pin
alert.text: Unveiled in Miami Beach. A permanent waterfront park location was announced but has not been named, and no installation has been reported. The map pin is a generic Miami point, not a statue site.

statues.name: New York
statues.note: Installed at the New York Stock Exchange by Twenty One Capital and announced by the NYSE on 10 Dec 2025. It is indoors and not open to the general public.
statues.access: Indoors at the New York Stock Exchange. NYSE tours are no longer offered to the general public, so the statue is not freely accessible.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue New York

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 10 Dec 2025, announced by the NYSE on X. The date matches the anniversary of Satoshi launching the Bitcoin mailing list on 10 Dec 2008.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Twenty One Capital (XXI, led by Jack Mallers), which had just listed on the NYSE.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: The NYSE called it "shared ground between emerging systems and established institutions… an artistic reflection on how new ideas become part of shared history". It uses the same disappearing-hacker design as the rest of the series.

story.label: Series
story.text: 6th of the series. Picozzi: "The 6th/21 statues of Satoshi Nakamoto found its home in the NYSE".

visit.getting_there:
The New York Stock Exchange is at 11 Wall St; its columned front faces Broad St. By subway, Broad St (J/Z) is closest. From Wall St (4/5), exit at Wall St and Broadway and walk east; from Wall St (2/3), exit at Wall St and William St and walk west (National Park Service; NYC Tourism).

Parking: street parking is extremely limited, and vehicle traffic is restricted around the exchange.
visit.exact_spot: Inside the NYSE building. Bitcoin Austria and Trending Topics place it in the NYSE museum; the exact room is unconfirmed.
visit.photo_tip: You can't photograph the statue itself without an invitation. The public shot is the NYSE façade on Broad Street; a tour-guide site says weekends are the least crowded.
visit.hours_access: Not publicly accessible. NYSE tours are no longer offered to the general public (they ended after 9/11), and visitors are admitted to the floor only with the Exchange's permission (NYC Tourism; NYSE Rule 37 memo). You can photograph the façade from Broad Street at any time.

sources.label: National Park Service: Federal Hall transit

statues.name: Fornelli
statues.note: Municipality-funded monument. The village has high Bitcoin merchant adoption.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Fornelli

visit.getting_there:
We couldn't verify any bus or rail service to Fornelli, and OpenStreetMap shows no public transport stops within about 1 km. Plan on arriving by car (local bus options are unverified).

Parking: OpenStreetMap marks a small car park right beside the piazza, about 15 m away. Fees and capacity are unverified.
visit.exact_spot: In Piazza Umberto I, Fornelli (province of Isernia, Molise), installed at the belvedere (Comune di Fornelli; ANSA). Pin: 41.60700, 14.14047 (OpenStreetMap node 12804537475).
visit.photo_tip:
This is not a Satoshigallery piece. It's by local crypto-artist Mattia Pannoni, but it has a similar effect: seen from the front, it seems to disappear (ANSA, quoting the artist). Take one frontal shot and one side shot to show it.

Generic tip (not from a source): the belvedere puts open sky behind the statue, which makes the see-through effect easier to read.
visit.hours_access: Outdoors in a public square. No hours are published. It should be viewable at any time, but that is our assumption and is unverified.

story.label: Artist
story.text: Mattia Pannoni, a local crypto-artist, who came up with the idea and made it.

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 1 May 2025 at 10:30, in Piazza Umberto I.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Funded entirely by the Comune di Fornelli (mayor Giovanni Tedeschi), on Pannoni's proposal.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: From the front the statue seems to vanish, "because Satoshi disappeared into nothing many years ago, and nobody knows his identity" (Pannoni). It was billed as Italy's first monument to Bitcoin and Satoshi, part of a plan to make Fornelli the "first Bitcoin village": 24 shops accepted bitcoin at the launch, in a village of about 1,800 residents.

story.label: Materials
story.text: Stainless steel (acciaio inox).

statues.name: Hong Kong
statues.place: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Wan Chai (unveiling venue)
statues.note: Unveiled on 20 Apr 2026 at the Hong Kong Web3 Festival at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Wan Chai, and donated to the Hong Kong SAR Government. No permanent display site has been reported, so its current location is unknown. The map pin marks the unveiling venue.
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Hong Kong

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 20 Apr 2026, at the Hong Kong Web3 Festival at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Wan Chai, in a donation ceremony.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: MicroBit Capital Management and HashKey Group, with several early industry figures. It was unveiled by Wilson Fung (MicroBit CEO) and Ryan Ru (HashKey Exchange CEO) and donated to the Hong Kong SAR Government to thank it for its regulatory environment.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: A contemplating figure with a notebook on its lap, nearly invisible from the front, "symbolizing Satoshi Nakamoto's dedication to decentralization, allowing the community to continue his legacy after his retirement". The base is engraved "To Hong Kong — In Math We Trust".

story.label: Materials
story.text: 304 stainless steel and weathering steel, about 1 cubic metre.

story.label: Series
story.text: 7th of the series (MicroBit: six had appeared before it).

story.label: Where it is now
story.text: Unknown. No permanent display location has been reported since the donation.

statues.statusLabel: Unveiled & donated (Apr 2026), no permanent site reported
statues.access: Current location unknown. No permanent display site has been reported since the statue was unveiled and donated in Apr 2026.

visit.getting_there:
Current location unknown, so check before you plan a trip. The statue was unveiled at the Hong Kong Web3 Festival in Hall 5BCDE of the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre (HKCEC), Wan Chai, and was then donated to the Hong Kong SAR Government.

For the HKCEC itself (only useful if the statue is shown there again): MTR Exhibition Centre station (East Rail line) Exit B3 or Wan Chai station (Island line) Exit A5, about a 10-minute walk, or the Star Ferry to Wan Chai pier (HKCEC).
visit.exact_spot: Unknown. Ownership passed to the Hong Kong SAR Government, and no permanent display location has been published (English and Chinese sources searched, Oct 2026). The map pin marks the unveiling venue, the HKCEC in Wan Chai (OpenStreetMap), not a confirmed current location.
visit.photo_tip: From the side it reads as a figure in deep contemplation with a notebook on its lap; head-on it is almost invisible. The base is engraved "To Hong Kong — In Math We Trust" (PANews).
visit.hours_access: Unknown. It was unveiled indoors in a convention hall during the festival; where and when it can be seen now has not been published.

alert.title: Donated, current location unknown
alert.text: Unveiled at the Hong Kong Web3 Festival (HKCEC, Wan Chai) and donated to the Hong Kong SAR Government. No permanent display site has been reported. The map pin marks the unveiling venue.

statues.name: Kranj Bitcoin Monument
statues.note: Often called the world’s first public Bitcoin monument. Large Corten steel structure featuring the Bitcoin “B” symbol (about 3 tonnes). Located on a roundabout near the city center. Linked to Slovenia’s early crypto scene (built by the Municipality of Kranj with support from 3fs and Bitstamp).
statues.label: Kranj Bitcoin Monument

visit.getting_there:
From OpenStreetMap (straight-line distances; routes and timetables unverified): Kranj bus station (Avtobusna postaja Kranj) is about 260 m away, and Kranj railway station (Železniška postaja Kranj) about 1.1 km.

Parking: OpenStreetMap shows a paid surface car park about 30 m from the roundabout.
visit.exact_spot: In the roundabout in front of the Kranj courthouse (RTV Slovenija). OpenStreetMap names it "Bitcoin krožišče" (Bitcoin roundabout), and the District Court (Okrožno sodišče v Kranju) is about 40 m away. Pin: 46.24636, 14.35781 (OpenStreetMap node 5903169142).
visit.photo_tip:
This isn't a see-through design. RTV Slovenija notes that the monument can best be seen from the air.

Generic tip (not from a source): shoot diagonally from a sidewalk corner so the tilted ring and the B symbol both read, and wait for a gap in traffic.
visit.hours_access: It sits in an active traffic circle, so view it from the surrounding sidewalks and don't walk into the roundabout. As a street monument it has no opening hours.

story.label: Artists
story.text: Idea by Selman Čorović; built in the workshop of Aleksander Frančeškin.

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: Tuesday 13 Mar 2018 at 3 p.m., by Mayor Boštjan Trilar and Jure Pirc, head of Bitcoin Slovenia.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Built by the Municipality of Kranj with support from 3fs and Bitstamp.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: A monument to blockchain technology: a circular rim around a B symbol, which the municipality says stands for blockchain technology rather than the cryptocurrency itself. Placing it in a roundabout symbolizes decentralized connections: "a nexus" with many paths, not a central point.

story.label: Materials
story.text: Corten steel, about 3 tonnes.

statues.name: Miami Bitcoin Bull
statues.place: Miami Dade College Wolfson Campus (NE 1st Ave & NE 4th St)
statues.note: Chrome/fiberglass robotic bull with blue laser eyes, commissioned by TradeStation and designed by Furio Tedeschi. Debuted at the Bitcoin 2022 conference in Miami Beach, then moved to its permanent home at Miami Dade College. A modern take on the Wall Street bull.
statues.label: Miami Bitcoin Bull

visit.getting_there:
Per OpenStreetMap, the Metromover's College North station is about 90 m away, and College Bayside about 200 m. A Miami-Dade Transit bus stop at NE 1st Avenue and NE 4th Street is about 55 m away. Metrorail Government Center (about 490 m) and Brightline MiamiCentral (about 400 m) are also close. Routes and schedules are unverified.

Parking: OpenStreetMap shows Miami Parking Authority Garage 3, paid, about 200 m away, plus Miami Dade College garages nearby whose public access is unverified.
visit.exact_spot: At the edge of Miami Dade College's Wolfson Campus in front of Building 1000, with its eyes facing NE 1st Avenue (MDC The Reporter). The site data puts it at NE 1st Ave and NE 4th St. Pin: 25.77820, -80.19186 (OpenStreetMap node 10677295005).
visit.photo_tip:
This isn't a see-through design. It's an 11-foot chrome-and-fiberglass bull with blue "laser" eyes.

Generic tips (not from a source): shoot low and slightly to one side so the horns and eyes stand out against the sky, and try dusk if the eyes are lit (unverified).
visit.hours_access: Outdoors on an open campus. MDC The Reporter described visitors walking up for selfies, and Local 10 News calls MDC the bull's permanent home. We found no posted hours, so viewing hours are unverified.

story.label: Artist

statues.name: Vienna
statues.place: Viertel Zwei (lakehead next to OMV Hoch Zwei)
statues.note: Unveiled Oct 14, 2026 by Bitcoin Austria for its 15th anniversary. Crowdfunded with over 1.3 BTC from 120+ donors (Genesis sponsor Bitpanda). Open to the public 24/7, near U2 Krieau.
statues.access: Outdoors at the head of the lake in Viertel Zwei, open to the public around the clock. Nearest U-Bahn: Krieau (U2).
statues.label: Satoshi Statue Vienna

visit.getting_there:
Take the U-Bahn U2 to Krieau, then walk toward the OMV Hoch Zwei building until you reach the start of the lake. Those are Bitcoin Austria's own directions.

Per OpenStreetMap, Krieau (U2) station is about 130 m from the statue in a straight line, and a Krieau bus stop is about 170 m away. Bus route numbers are unverified.

Parking: the paid multi-storey Messe Parkhaus D is about 180 m away (OpenStreetMap). Rates and opening hours are unverified.
visit.exact_spot: At the head of the lake (Seeanfang) in Viertel Zwei, right next to the OMV Hoch Zwei building, 1020 Vienna (Leopoldstadt). Pin: 48.21351, 16.41363 (OpenStreetMap node 14287266624).
visit.photo_tip:
Bitcoin Austria says the figure is clearly visible from the side and almost invisible from the front, so take one shot from each angle to show the disappearing effect. Their party trick is to have a friend stand behind the statue. Everyone in front then sees that person's reflection in Satoshi's face, as in "We are all Satoshi".

Generic tip (not from a source): the 61 steel profiles are mirror-polished, so watch for glare and your own reflection in direct sun.
visit.hours_access: Outdoors and publicly accessible at any time (Bitcoin Austria: "jederzeit öffentlich zugänglich", "Öffentlich, im Freien"). No admission fee is mentioned. Bitcoin Austria's "free entry" note was for the unveiling event.

story.label: Artist
story.text: Valentina Picozzi (Satoshigallery).

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: 14 Oct 2026 at 17:00, hosted by Der Fil (Philipp Horwath), for Bitcoin Austria's 15th anniversary.

story.label: Commissioned by
story.text: Bitcoin Austria, crowdfunded from Dec 2025 to Aug 2026: more than 120 private donors plus companies gave over 1.3 BTC (about €97k). The Genesis sponsor was Bitpanda, with Incrementum, Enzinger Steuerberatung, Bitkern, Was Bitcoin bringt, Stadler Partner, Bitcredit, Validvent and Viertel Zwei. Extra donations fund maintenance and insurance.

story.label: What the design means
story.text: Seated hacker with a laptop on his lap, built from 61 thin mirror-polished stainless-steel profiles with gaps between them (a technique taken from sculptor Julian Voss-Andreae), on a Corten-steel base. It is clear from the side and almost invisible head-on, standing for Satoshi's anonymity and retreat from public life. Someone standing behind it is reflected in the face, so "We are all Satoshi". The "cliché" hacker deliberately honours all the developers who built Bitcoin. It is deliberately not a portrait, so it stays valid even if Satoshi is ever identified (Tobias Girstmair). Vienna was chosen as the home of the Austrian School of economics (Menger, Mises, Hayek).

story.label: Materials
story.text: 61 mirror-polished stainless-steel profiles on a Corten-steel base; the figure is about 90 cm tall, about 1.5 m with the base.

story.label: Title
story.text: “El Génesis de Satoshi Nakamoto”.

story.label: Artists
story.text: Ricardo Alonso and Celeste Difabio Videla.

story.label: Unveiled
story.text: Thursday 29 Oct 2026, in the evening, at Polo DOT in Buenos Aires, at the opening cocktail of LABITCONF 2026.

story.label: What it is
story.text: A stainless-steel and glass structure measuring 2.40 × 2.40 × 2.40 m, inspired by Bitcoin’s genesis block, the first block of the chain. Per the organisers, it combines architecture, light and reflections so visitors can walk around it and see it from different angles.

story.label: How it came about
story.text: Selected in the monument category of the Premio B·Arte 2025 art competition. A project of the NGO Bitcoin Argentina, funded by the Fundación Bitcoin Iberoamérica, with Polo DOT as the venue.

visit.exact_spot:
At Polo DOT, the office complex next to the DOT Baires shopping centre (Vedia 3600, Saavedra, Buenos Aires). The organisers’ press release places it in the complex’s Workplace area; the exact spot hasn’t been published.

Pin: the Polo DOT office park in OpenStreetMap (-34.5470, -58.4893), about 135 m from the DOT Baires shopping centre.
visit.hours_access: Public visiting hours haven’t been published yet. The organisers say anyone who wants to will be able to visit, but no hours or conditions have been announced. Check with Bitcoin Argentina or LABITCONF before you go.

upcoming21.summary: Community fundraiser by Jednadvacet.org (The Malahar Network z.s.), launched 12 June 2026 at BTC Prague. The 1 BTC base goal (the fixed price of the statue from Satoshi Gallery) was reached; the maximum target is 1.3 BTC to cover shipping, customs, VAT and installation. On 10 Aug 2026 the organizers reported about 1.26 BTC raised, said the location was being negotiated with Prague City Hall, and expected delivery around the turn of the year (2026/27).
